metadata.title: Private Security Services ERP Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: How the security ERP must change under convention changes, regulation, technology and expansion.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: One Spanish ERP with a single convention hard-coded, rosters in a grid, paper rounds and incident logs, invoices from contracted rather than covered hours.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Versioned conventions per country, licence-aware roster solver, event-based presence and rounds that feed payroll, billing and client proof, and country packs for regulators and e-invoicing.

stressors.name: A new state security collective agreement changes premiums and annual hours
stressors.detection: Convenio negotiations, union statements, labour claims.
stressors.attractor: Payroll, quotes and rosters are wrong from the effective date.
stressors.businessReaction: Release versioned convention tables ahead of the date, re-cost quotes and re-check rosters.
stressors.residue: Conventions as versioned reference data shared by costing, rostering and payroll.

stressors.name: Clients replace some static guarding with remote video and alarms
stressors.detection: Tenders mixing guards with remote monitoring; declining static hours.
stressors.attractor: Hours-based revenue and rosters shrink; incidents come from sensors.
stressors.businessReaction: Model mixed services, ingest alarm events as incidents and bill per outcome.
stressors.residue: Service model beyond hours; incident intake from devices.

stressors.name: A Latin American regulator changes reporting rules
stressors.attractor: Reports and payroll no longer comply in one country.
stressors.businessReaction: Isolate country rules in packs and release them independently.
stressors.residue: Country packs with independent release cycles.

stressors.name: A multinational client mandates a global guard-tour platform
stressors.attractor: Local ERP loses the field layer.
stressors.businessReaction: Offer APIs to import rounds and incidents from third-party platforms while keeping payroll and billing.
